paper_title: Using the Sun and the Moon as Source masses and the Earth's Rotation as a Modulation to Search for Exotic Spin-Dependent Interactions at Astronomical Distances
suggested_experiment_name: Sun/Moon-based exotic spin-dependent interaction search using Earth's rotation modulation
coupling_convention: g_S^N * g_P^n (dimensionless product of scalar and pseudoscalar couplings), as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper constrains three types of exotic spin-dependent interactions at astronomical distances (10^7–10^14 m) by analyzing sidereal modulation in existing comagnetometer data (Ref. [45], 129Xe+3He). Three coupling products extracted: (1) scalar-pseudoscalar |g_S^N g_P^n| with best limit ~1.6×10^-35 at λ>10^12 m (improves previous combined astrophysical-laboratory limit by ~70×); (2) vector-axial-vector |g_V^N g_A^n| with best limit ~7.1×10^-59 at λ>10^12 m (improves by ~12 orders of magnitude); (3) axial-axial-vector |g_A^N g_A^n| with best limit ~8.1×10^-31 at λ>10^12 m (first constraint at astronomical scales). Data points represent mass-independent (flat) bounds over stated ranges; encoded as horizontal lines per instructions. Interaction range λ = ℏ/(m_φ c) relates to mediator mass m_φ. Paper also constrains Hari-Dass spin-gravity interactions (α₁, α₂). Confidence 0.85 reflects clear coupling type identification and explicit numerical limits in text, though data extraction from figures and text descriptions rather than tables. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 38)) | Vision: Extracted lower boundary of exclusion region from FIG. 2 (left panel, Moon source). The x-axis represents interaction range λ in meters, converted to mass via m = ℏc/λ ≈ 1.24e-7 eV·m / λ. The y-axis shows |g_S^N g_P^n| directly. The excluded region (dark gray) is ABOVE the boundary curve. Boundary traced from low mass (~1 m, ~1e-28 coupling) following the Moon constraint curve upward with increasing steepness, reaching ~1e10 m (~1e-23 coupling) at the kink where the curve transitions. The plot shows three constraints: Astro Limit (dashed), This work-using the Moon (solid left), and This work-using the Sun (solid right). Sampled more densely near the kink region (10^9-10^11 m) where slope changes significantly. The coupling type is MonopoleDipole because the paper explicitly discusses scalar coupling g_S^N at one vertex and pseudoscalar coupling g_P^n at the polarized neutron vertex, with their product |g_S^N g_P^n| plotted on the y-axis. | Calibration: No calibration needed
